appraisal_events.evidence: Bergotte m'avait parlé du docteur du Boulbon comme d'un médecin qui... s'adapterait à la singularité de mon intelligence; Charcot avant de mourir avait prédit qu'il régnerait sur la neurologie et la psychiatrie... je suppliai ma mère de le faire venir... Du Boulbon appelé donna tort... à ma grand'mère.
appraisal_events.explanation: Endorsement from Bergotte and the reported prediction of Charcot build du Boulbon into a figure of near-limitless authority for the narrator, in implicit contrast to Cottard's tactless joke and ineffective milk regimen, culminating in du Boulbon's confident authority to overrule the grandmother's own account of her condition.

appraisal_events.evidence: "Ah! je ne sais pas, c'est très possible", dit Françoise qui... entendait pour la première fois le nom de Charcot... Ses «c'est possible», ses «peut-être», ses «je ne sais pas» étaient exaspérants en pareil cas.
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator directly criticizes Françoise's habitual, uninformed hedging as exasperating pretension to an opinion she has no basis for.

status_effects.explanation: He is built up through prestigious endorsement (Bergotte, Charcot) into an object of near-limitless confidence and authority for the narrator.
His glib joke about a 'maladie diplomatique' and his ineffective milk regimen are set against du Boulbon's rising authority, locally diminishing him by comparison.
Despite her witty self-defense via Mme de Sévigné's letter, du Boulbon's professional judgment overrides her own account of her condition, giving him the last word.
Her noncommittal, uninformed responses are explicitly called exasperating by the narrator, marking a clear negative judgment of her conversational credibility.

ambiguities: The narrator explicitly generalizes that medicine as a whole is 'un compendium des erreurs successives et contradictoires des médecins,' which somewhat softens how much of Cottard's ineffective treatment should be read as personal incompetence versus the fallibility of the discipline generally.
